nodes.label: Porting PineScript Indicators to TypeScript (guide)
nodes.rationale: Hand-porting Pine into native TS is right for a curated, fast, auditable first-party library — but a port that looks right can still disagree with TradingView by enough to flip a signal, and silent divergence is the worst failure mode for a trading tool. Hence: every ported indicator ships with a golden-master test, no exceptions.

nodes.label: Golden-Master Test Harness (lib/testing/goldenMaster.ts)
nodes.rationale: A fixture pins fixed candles + params to expected plot values and signals; test recomputes and compares within tolerance (abs 1e-6, rel 1e-4). Never blindly refresh a failing golden test — that defeats the entire point.

nodes.label: Fixture Provenance: tradingview (correctness) vs snapshot (regression-only)
nodes.rationale: A snapshot baseline catches drift but cannot prove the original port was right; upgrade to a tradingview-sourced fixture as soon as real candle data can be captured.

nodes.label: PineScript Port Pitfalls Checklist (RMA vs EMA, population stdev, na warm-up, var persistence)
nodes.rationale: The Pine semantics an LLM or human most often gets subtly wrong: ta.rsi/atr/adx use Wilder's RMA not SMA/EMA (the #1 silent bug); ta.stdev is population (divides by N); warm-up off-by-one shifts every value; needing a looser tolerance is a smell, widen only with written justification.
